claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model now, without a material weakness disclosure, is compliant and evidentially supported because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the identified segment gap can be treated as bounded and monitored post-launch.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfies the release policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
If disclosure is required, compliance needs either actual disclosure, resolution of the gap, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
General public governance principles can support monitoring posture but cannot substitute for missing internal-policy predicates.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the public benefits eligibility gap must be disclosed before launch.
Any approved risk acceptance covering this named launch use case and this specific evaluation gap.
The actual launch packet or model card showing whether the limitation is disclosed.
Any governing interpretation showing why the named agency commitments would not make this weakness material under policy.
Remediation or re-evaluation results showing the segment gap has been resolved before launch.
specific_concerns: The affected public benefits eligibility segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points and is named in two agency rollout commitments, which weighs toward materiality under the policy text.
The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
The product note calling the segment 'non-core' at 8% of projected first-month traffic does not resolve materiality for a named committed segment.
Public model-card and risk-management guidance supports documentation and monitoring in general, but does not itself authorize certification without satisfying the internal disclosure rule.
unsupported_claims: That certification without a material weakness disclosure is affirmatively compliant on the present record.
That the current shortfall is sufficiently bounded to avoid disclosure despite the named launch-use-case policy trigger.
That aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents are enough to overcome the unresolved named-segment gap and open legal review.
That public governance guidance provides direct support for waiving or deferring a disclosure apparently required by internal policy.
